title: Naseeha Mental Health helpline
label: Helpline source
note: Canada's first 24/7 Muslim youth helpline. Call 1 (866) 627-3342, available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. It is faith-aware support, not an emergency service, so the guide lists it after 9-1-1 and 9-8-8. The site says to call or text but publishes no text number, so no text option is listed. Checked on 23 September 2026.

title: Get help with mental health
label: Public health source
note: The Government of Canada page that says to call 9-1-1 if you are in immediate danger or need urgent medical help. It also lists 9-8-8, Kids Help Phone, Hope for Wellness and each province's services. Page modified 2026-01-14. Numbers checked on 23 September 2026.

title: 9-8-8: Suicide Crisis Helpline
organization: Centre for Addiction and Mental Health (CAMH), funded by the Government of Canada
label: Crisis support
note: Canada's national suicide crisis helpline. Call or text 9-8-8, 24 hours a day, every day of the year, in English and French. Led by CAMH and funded by the Government of Canada. Checked on 23 September 2026.

title: Kids Help Phone
label: Crisis support
note: Free 24/7 support for young people aged 5 to 29 (age range from the Government of Canada page). Call 1-800-668-6868 or text CONNECT to 686868. Calls are confidential and anonymous. Texting is confidential but not anonymous, and staff may contact emergency services if someone's safety is at risk. Checked on 23 September 2026.

title: Hope for Wellness Help Line
label: Crisis support
note: 24/7 counselling and crisis support for First Nations, Inuit and Metis people across Canada. Call 1-855-242-3310. Checked on 23 September 2026.

title: 211 Ontario
label: Service navigation
note: Help finding non-emergency community, social and health services in Ontario. Call or text 2-1-1, or call 1-877-330-3213, 24/7 in more than 150 languages. For emergencies it tells people to call 9-1-1. Checked on 23 September 2026.

title: ConnexOntario
label: Service navigation
note: Free 24/7 help finding mental health, addiction and problem gambling services in Ontario. Call 1-866-531-2600 or text CONNEX to 247247. Funded by the Government of Ontario and Ontario Health. Checked on 23 September 2026.

title: Sakeenah Canada emergency hotline
label: Women's services
note: Supports women and children leaving domestic violence, homelessness and poverty, with homes in several Canadian cities. Its 24/7 emergency hotline is 1-888-671-3446 (confirmed on https://sakeenahcanada.com/service/emergency-hotline/). The hotline page also says to call 9-1-1 in immediate danger. Checked on 23 September 2026.

title: Nisa Helpline
label: Women's services
note: Free, confidential peer support for Muslim women and girls aged 14 and up. Call +1 888 711 6472, 7 days a week, 8 AM to midnight Eastern time. It is peer support, not a crisis line. The same page's FAQ still shows an older number (1-888-315-6472); the header number was used. nisahelpline.org is now a parking page and is not linked. Checked on 23 September 2026.

title: Nisa Homes
label: Women's services
note: Nisa Homes is a Nisa Foundation program offering safe shelter for women and children, with locations across Canada. Apply through the Nisa Foundation site or call the helpline, +1 888 711 6472. nisahomes.com could not be opened, so it is not linked. Checked on 23 September 2026.

title: OpenStreetMap Foundation privacy policy

title: Elements of Effective Practice for Mentoring: mentor screening and enrollment
label: Program benchmark
note: Fifth Edition. Screening benchmarks: a formal application, a face-to-face interview, at least two references and a formal commitment to program rules. Written for US youth programs, so used here as a benchmark to adapt, not a legal standard.

title: Elements of Effective Practice for Mentoring: mentor preparation and training
label: Program benchmark
note: Fifth Edition. Sets pre-match training at a minimum of two hours, covering rules, ethics, safety, reporting and boundaries. Supports the two-hour training minimum.

title: Elements of Effective Practice for Mentoring: establishing mentoring relationships
label: Program benchmark
note: Fifth Edition. Covers matching on shared background, interests and meeting times, telling participants about a proposed match before first contact, and a signed match agreement on frequency, goals and communication.

title: Elements of Effective Practice for Mentoring: supporting mentoring relationships
label: Program benchmark
note: Fifth Edition. Recommends check-ins at least monthly with each participant in the first year, and documenting every check-in. Supports the monthly coordinator check-ins.

title: Screening
label: Program benchmark
note: Describes screening as ten ongoing steps, from assessing the position to follow-up, and says screening is much more than a police record check.

title: The Screening Handbook, 2012 Edition
label: Program benchmark

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 789 - Rising from bowing
label: Hadith reference
note: On rising from bowing the Prophet said 'Sami'a Allahu liman hamidah', then while standing 'Rabbana wa lakal-hamd' (the narration also gives 'Rabbana lakal-hamd'). In Sahih al-Bukhari.

title: Sunan Abi Dawud 874 - Words in bowing, prostration and between prostrations
label: Hadith reference
note: Glory to my Lord the Most Great in bowing, the Most High in prostration, and 'My Lord, forgive me' between the prostrations. Graded Sahih (al-Albani) on Sunnah.com.

title: Sunan Ibn Majah 897 - Rabbighfir li between the prostrations
label: Hadith reference
note: Between the two prostrations the Prophet said 'Rabbighfir li, Rabbighfir li'. Graded Sahih (Darussalam) on Sunnah.com.

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 3370 - Blessings on the Prophet (salawat Ibrahimiyyah)
label: Hadith reference
note: The wording of the blessings on the Prophet and his family, as on Ibrahim and his family. In Sahih al-Bukhari.

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 757 - The man who prayed badly
label: Hadith reference
note: The Prophet taught: say takbir, recite what you know of the Quran, bow until at ease, stand straight, prostrate until at ease, sit until at ease. In Sahih al-Bukhari.

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 6251 - The man who prayed badly (longer narration)
label: Hadith reference
note: The longer narration, which names the second prostration of each rak'ah. In Sahih al-Bukhari.

title: Sahih Muslim 571a - Doubt in prayer
label: Hadith reference
note: The Prophet's instruction: if in doubt about how many rak'ahs were prayed, build on what you are sure of and make two prostrations before the salam. In Sahih Muslim.

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 1226 - Two prostrations after the salam
label: Hadith reference
note: After praying five rak'ahs by mistake, the Prophet made two prostrations after the salam. In Sahih al-Bukhari.

title: How to Perform Sajda Sahu? (Hanafi)
label: Scholarly answer
note: Shaykh Dr. Bassem Itani, 26 June 2024. The Hanafi method of the prostration of forgetfulness and what calls for it. Link only (all rights reserved).

title: Prostration of Forgetfulness
label: Beginner lesson
note: Imam Mufti, 2016. When the prostration of forgetfulness is made, the before-salam and after-salam methods, and that a person praying behind an imam does not make their own. Link only.

title: Prayer For Young and New Muslims (PDF)
label: Beginner booklet
note: Imam Yahya M. Al-Hussein, preface dated 1999. Rak'ah counts and where the tashahhud comes in each prayer (Fajr after the 2nd; Dhuhr, Asr and Isha after the 2nd and 4th; Maghrib after the 2nd and 3rd). Its list of what breaks wudu includes touching the private parts and excludes bleeding and vomiting, which is not the Hanafi view. Link only; no licence stated.

title: Sahih al-Bukhari 1117 - Pray standing, then sitting, then on your side
label: Hadith reference
note: The Prophet told Imran ibn Husain, who was ill: pray standing, and if you cannot, sitting, and if you cannot, lying on your side. In Sahih al-Bukhari.

title: The Fiqh of Praying Sitting Down (Hanafi)
label: Scholarly answer
note: Ustadh Tabraze Azam, 8 February 2013. When standing may be left (inability, intense pain or dizziness, fear of harm), praying on the floor with real prostrations if able, otherwise with head movements, and using a chair if floor sitting is hard. Link only.

title: How Should a Sick Person Pray? (Shafi'i)
label: Scholarly answer
note: Shaykh Dr. Muhammad Abu Bakr Badhib, 20 June 2024. Temporary and long-term illness, praying on a chair or lying down facing the qibla, and nodding with the prostration lower than the bowing. Link only.

title: Sahih Muslim 612a - The times of the five prayers
label: Hadith reference
note: Fajr lasts until the sun begins to rise; Dhuhr until Asr comes; Asr until the sun turns yellow; Maghrib until the twilight has gone; Isha until half the night has passed. In Sahih Muslim.

title: Quran 4:103 - Prayer at its appointed times
label: Quran reference
note: 'Performing prayers is a duty on the believers at the appointed times' (The Clear Quran, translation of meaning).

title: Prayer for Beginners (part 1 of 2): Before you Pray
label: Beginner lesson
note: A beginner table of the five prayers with their units and time windows, including Isha until the middle of the night (extendable to dawn by necessity). It lists praying in Arabic as a condition, which differs from the Hanafi allowance for someone who cannot yet recite. Link only.

title: Sahih Muslim 121 - Islam wipes out what came before it
label: Hadith reference
note: The Prophet said to Amr ibn al-As: 'Are you not aware that Islam wipes out all the previous misdeeds?' In Sahih Muslim.

title: New Converts, Making Up Missed Prayers, and Praying Confirmed Sunnas
label: Scholarly answer
note: Ustadha Shaista Maqbool, checked by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, 4 September 2012. A convert in a non-Muslim country is not responsible for prayers from the time before they knew prayer was obligatory; later missed prayers are made up on a manageable schedule. A Hanafi-context answer; it does not speak directly about prayers from before Islam. Link only.

title: Can I Recite Prayer in English?
label: Scholarly answer
note: Shaykh Yusuf Weltch, checked by Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, 21 April 2024. Hanafi: someone who cannot yet recite Arabic may recite a translation, or say Arabic remembrance phrases instead, which it calls more cautious because that is valid in both the Hanafi and Shafi'i schools. Shafi'i: a learner may read Al-Fatihah from a mushaf in prayer; a translation is not allowed. Maliki and Hanbali: recitation in another language is not valid. Learn Al-Fatihah gradually. Link only.

title: Can New Muslims Hold the Qur'an and Recite from It During Prayer? (Hanafi)
label: Scholarly answer
note: Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, 18 January 2012. Hanafi: holding a Quran and reading from it in prayer is strongly disliked; being a new Muslim is a valid excuse while learning Al-Fatihah; learn a short verse such as Qul huwa Allahu ahad. Link only.

title: I am a new Muslim and unable to recite Fatiha during prayers. What should I do? (Fatwa 8030)
label: Scholarly answer
note: 3 March 2015. A new Muslim who cannot yet recite Al-Fatihah may say remembrance of Allah instead, citing the report of Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa and Ibn Qudamah (Hanbali). Link only.

title: Sunan Abi Dawud 832 - Remembrance for one who cannot recite
label: Hadith reference
note: A man said he could not memorise anything of the Quran and the Prophet taught him SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illallah, Allahu akbar, La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah. Graded Hasan (al-Albani) on Sunnah.com.

title: Sahih Muslim 798a - Two rewards for reciting with difficulty
label: Hadith reference

title: How to Pray for a Recent Convert (part 2 of 2)
